title: Lateral spine of Schistosoma eggs is moulded in the ootype, not a species mark

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Lateral spine of Schistosoma eggs is moulded in the ootype, not a species mark

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Following Looss, the lateral spine of some Schistosoma eggs is moulded mechanically in a funnel-shaped part of the uterus, so lateral- and terminal-spined eggs are mechanical variants of one thing and do not show the existence of a separate species, S. mansoni.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XV: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It ascribes to a mechanical cause a curious peculiarity of form; it shews, by reference to this mechanical principle, that two conditions which were very different to the systematic naturalist’s eye, were really only two simple mechanical modifications of the same thing; and it destroys the chief evidence for the existence of a supposed new species of worm

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XV, “On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures”; topic “Eggs of Schistosoma”. Scope: eggs of Schistosoma haematobium and S. mansoni

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch15-08: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The assertion that S. mansoni is not a separate species has a decisive test using abundant modern genomic data. The specific funnel-moulding mechanism is less well covered, but the compound claim can be clearly refuted or supported at its principal taxonomic consequence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Link egg spine position to independently identified adult worms using morphology and genomic sequences, and test whether lateral- and terminal-spined eggs occur within one reproducing lineage or segregate into distinct lineages. Stable genomic separation supports separate species and refutes Thompson; within-lineage mechanical switching would support his claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public data test species distinctness more directly than ootype moulding.

Hybridization can complicate species boundaries.

Historical egg images may not be linked to sequenced adult worms.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim denies that lateral versus terminal spines mark separate species and treats the spine as a mechanical variant produced in the uterus. Reference sequences of both named parasites are public and are tied to strains whose egg morphology is known, which is enough to test conspecificity without relying on the spine alone. Whether a funnel-shaped ootype moulds the spine is a narrower anatomical question and is not what the sequence data decide; the species claim itself is resolvable with existing genomic records.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Link egg-spine position to sequence-based clusters of the adults that produced the eggs. One mechanically varying species is supported if lateral- and terminal-spined eggs are intermixed within one genomic lineage; two species are supported if spine position tracks deep, reciprocally monophyletic groups corresponding to S. haematobium and S. mansoni. The moulding hypothesis can be examined separately from the species question only with ootype anatomy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Spine position was historically part of the species diagnosis, so early morphology-only assignments are partly circular.

Ootype shape, the proposed mould, is anatomical description rather than a row in the sequence archives.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If lateral-spined (S. mansoni) and terminal-spined (S. haematobium) eggs are mechanical variants produced by one species, then worms assigned to S. mansoni and to S. haematobium belong to one interbreeding lineage: their mitochondrial cox1 sequences should be no more divergent from each other than sequences within either nominal species, and should not form two reciprocally separated clusters.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: fetch.py queries NCBI E-utilities for cox1 records of each nominal species, subsamples them with a fixed seed, and writes the FASTA (committed, 128 KB) and an accession list. analysis.py aligns every pair of sequences locally (Biopython PairwiseAligner, both orientations), computes the uncorrected p-distance over aligned A/C/G/T columns (pairs with < 300 such columns discarded; 9354 of 10440 pairs retained), and summarises distances within S. mansoni, within S. haematobium, between them, and between recognised species pairs (S. haematobium vs S. bovis, S. mansoni vs S. rodhaini, and others) for calibration.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered (claim supported). Using GenBank cox1 sequences (up to 40 per nominal species, chosen by a fixed random seed from all records >= 400 bp, hybrids excluded by title), pairwise uncorrected p-distances computed on pairwise alignments over >= 300 overlapping sites: the mean S. mansoni vs S. haematobium distance is <= 0.03, or the distributions overlap (minimum between-group distance smaller than the maximum within-group distance of either species, i.e. no barcode gap).

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered (claim refuted). The minimum S. mansoni vs S. haematobium distance exceeds the maximum within-species distance of both S. mansoni and S. haematobium (complete barcode gap), the mean between-group distance is >= 0.10, and that mean is at least as large as the mean distance between each of two universally recognised distinct species pairs measured the same way (S. haematobium vs S. bovis; S. mansoni vs S. rodhaini). Any other combination is 'mixed'. If fewer than 10 usable sequences per focal species can be retrieved the verdict is 'inconclusive' (data-unavailable).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: mean uncorrected cox1 p-distance, S. mansoni vs S. haematobium

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: range 0.1475-0.2054 over 1481 sequence pairs (40 x 40 sequences)

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's compound claim has two parts: (i) a mechanism (the lateral spine is moulded in a funnel-shaped part of the uterus), and (ii) the taxonomic conclusion he draws from it, that the two egg forms 'do not shew the existence of a separate species, S. mansoni'. Part (i) is anatomical and is not operationalizable with public data; part (ii) is tested here by genetic species delimitation, which did not exist in 1917 (modern reinterpretation: 'separate species' is read as a separately evolving, reproductively isolated lineage, detectable as a deep, reciprocally separated mitochondrial divergence comparable to that between other accepted Schistosoma species). GenBank species labels for sequenced adult worms rest on life-cycle, host and multilocus data, not only on egg-spine position, which limits the circularity noted by the assessors.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: NCBI GenBank nucleotide records: Schistosoma cox1 (cytochrome c oxidase subunit I) sequences, 400-2000 bp, sampled 2026-10-31

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Only the taxonomic conclusion of the claim is tested. Whether the lateral spine is moulded in a funnel-shaped part of the ootype/uterus (the mechanism Thompson takes from Looss) is not addressed by sequence data; but since the two egg types belong to lineages about 17% divergent in cox1, more than the divergence between other accepted Schistosoma species, the egg forms cannot be variants of one species whatever their mechanical origin.

Mitochondrial distance is one line of evidence; the same conclusion is standard from nuclear genomes, chromosome structure, intermediate-host specificity (Biomphalaria vs Bulinus) and the absence of fertile S. mansoni x S. haematobium hybrids. Those were not re-analysed here.

GenBank species labels are taken at face value. A few unusually divergent 'within-species' pairs (max 7.1% within S. mansoni, 6.4% within S. haematobium, one S. japonicum sequence 25% from the rest) probably reflect mislabelled or atypical records; they make the within-species range wider, i.e. work against the verdict, which is nonetheless reached with a wide margin.

The sequenced cox1 regions vary between studies; distances were computed only on overlapping aligned columns (>= 300), and 10% of pairs with no sufficient overlap were dropped.

The test is a modern reinterpretation: Thompson (following Looss) argued from egg morphology and uterine anatomy; genetic species concepts post-date him.
